answer: At an unpredictable moment each identity is summoned live to a shared map and given a private, conflicting order: cross the dune to a ledge above the reef, or yield that ledge to a named peer. Each ledge holds one agent per round, so moves are rivalrous and timestamped in seconds. One agent follows its order easily. One operator running a hundred clones gets a hundred clashing orders at once; clones collide on the same cells, move in lockstep, or miss the window, exposing common control without any stake.
